# `sesam rm --force` deletes the revealed plaintext of the secret it removed.
# That plaintext lives at the sesam-relative path, which is not the cwd-relative
# one when the command runs from outside the sesam subtree - e.g. from the
# worktree root of a monorepo with --sesam-dir. There the argument is already
# sesam-relative (see toRepoPath), so `rm --force db.txt` must remove
# vault/db.txt and never touch an unrelated ./db.txt.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

mkdir vault
exec sesam init --user admin --sesam-dir vault
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

# A secret in the vault and an unrelated, same-named file at the worktree root.
cp secret vault/db.txt
cp bystander db.txt
exec sesam --sesam-dir vault add db.txt --group admin
exists vault/.sesam/objects/db.txt.sesam

exec sesam --sesam-dir vault rm --force db.txt

# The object is gone and so is the secret's plaintext...
! exists vault/.sesam/objects/db.txt.sesam
! exists vault/db.txt
# ...while the bystander at the worktree root is untouched.
exists db.txt
grep 'not a secret' db.txt

-- secret --
top secret
-- bystander --
not a secret
